applicableAreas: Buildings and permanent structures throughout the site
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly shows overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) running along Valley View Road (western boundary) and the northern property boundary, with utility poles marked. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows eight multi-story residential buildings (ranging from 33'-5" to 36'-1" in height) positioned on the site. The overhead electric utility line is labeled '----OHE----' on the site plan running along the Valley View Road frontage (southern boundary). However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on Sheet 9 showing the horizontal distance from the outside conductor of the overhead line to any building face or structure. No building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions were found in the submitted plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, and secondary conductors. The regulation defines this as a vertical plane extending infinitely upward from a point 7.5 feet from the conductor. The site plan shows buildings within reasonable proximity to the overhead lines along Valley View Road, but the applicant has provided no dimensional evidence that the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal clearance is maintained. The absence of clearance annotations and dimensions constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance. Per the grouping documentation, clearance dimensions must be labeled on plans with dimension lines originating from the actual outside conductor location (not pole centerline).
findings.comment: Proposed buildings do not show measured clearance dimensions from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. All buildings with potential clearance concerns require clearance dimension annotations on site plan and building elevation sheets, measured from the outside (outermost) conductor, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.

findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents existing overhead utility lines running along the property boundary and service drop. The proposed buildings range from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1" in height. A complete set of building elevation sheets showing the surveyed elevation of the existing overhead conductors is not present in the submitted site plan set. While general notes on Sheet 3 reference benchmarks (B.M. #1 at 678.52' and B.M. #2 at 681.08' NAVD 88), these are general site control points, not surveyed overhead conductor elevations. No building elevation exhibits were found that show the actual conductor elevation overlaid with the building profile to verify vertical clearances.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Documentation Requirements section, 'Profile plans: Engineered, sealed profile drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and building features, including overhangs, balconies, and canopies, with dimensioned clearances' are required. The grouping cites UCM § 1.10.3 as requiring permanent clearances and explicitly states that clearance verification requires 'surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors included on building elevation sheets.' Without surveyed conductor elevation data on building elevation sheets, the applicant cannot demonstrate that the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or other required clearances are met.
findings.comment: Building elevation sheets do not show surveyed elevations of existing overhead electric conductors. Sealed building elevation exhibits are required for all buildings with potential proximity to overhead lines, showing the surveyed elevation of the outside conductor and dimensioned clearances from the conductor to building faces and projections.

applicableAreas: Site plan sections and elevation views
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly identifies overhead utility lines with the notation 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road and the northern property boundary. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) both show overhead electric lines (labeled 'OHE' or '----OHE----') but NO dimension lines or clearance annotations extending from the outside conductor to the outer edges of any buildings, projections, site features, or structures. No section views or profile exhibits were found showing the cross-section relationship between the overhead conductor and site features. The landscape plan shows trees proposed near the OHE line but with no distance callouts or species specifications.
findings.reasoning: The grouping explicitly states: 'Common Violation Patterns: Clearances measured from pole instead of conductor... Dimension annotations read "10'-0" from pole" instead of "15'-0" from outside conductor"' and 'Missing profile plans: Site plan shows building and overhead lines in plan view only, no elevation/section view; no surveyed mid-span clearance data; cannot verify vertical clearances meet requirements.' UCM § 1.10.3 requires permanent clearances, which must be demonstrated through dimension callouts showing measurement from the outside (outermost) conductor to the building edge. The complete absence of these dimensions constitutes a deficiency.
findings.comment: Section and plan view exhibits do not show dimensions from the outside electric conductor to the outermost edges of proposed buildings, building projections, and other site features. Enlarged plan details and section views are required showing dimension lines originating from the outside conductor and extending to all building faces and structures within potential clearance distance, demonstrating compliance with the 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement.

applicableAreas: Proposed driveway intersection with overhead utility line at Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows an overhead utility line labeled 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road (western boundary). The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows a proposed driveway at the bottom left (Valley View Road frontage) area. Per the vision analysis of Sheet 9, the proposed driveway 'crosses directly under the horizontal ----OHE---- line' along Valley View Road. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows the finished floor elevations and site grades but does not annotate the vertical clearance dimensions at the driveway location where the overhead line crosses. No registered surveyor data showing mid-span clearance measurements is provided. The roadway grade elevations are not dimensioned relative to the overhead line height.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 specifies: 'Driveway and parking without truck traffic: 16 feet minimum vertical clearance; Roads, streets, alleys, and areas with truck traffic: 18 feet minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments.' The grouping documentation notes this is a 'Common Violation Pattern: Inadequate service-drop clearances: Driveway grade shown within 15-16 feet of overhead service drop without mid-span clearance verification; service drop sag at maximum load/temperature may contact vehicles.' Since the proposed driveway crosses under the overhead line, vertical clearance must be verified through surveyed mid-span clearance data showing the lowest point of the conductor at maximum sag. The absence of this documentation constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance.
findings.reasoning2: The Site Plan Release Notes (Block 7 on Sheet 9) state: 'For driveway construction: The owner is responsible for all costs for relocation of, or damage to utilities.' This note is an acknowledgment of the utility risk but does not substitute for required clearance verification.
findings.comment: The proposed driveway crosses the existing overhead electric line at Valley View Road. No section views, surveyed mid-span clearance measurements, or vertical clearance dimension annotations are provided to demonstrate the minimum 16-foot (or 18-foot for truck traffic areas) vertical clearance from the lowest point of the overhead line to the finished driveway grade. A registered surveyor's survey showing mid-span clearance is required, with results documented on section views and profile sheets.

applicableAreas: All clearance dimension annotations on site plan
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows multiple utility poles and overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) on the property. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows the overhead electric line (OHE) running along the Valley View Road frontage. However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on the plans. The grouping documentation emphasizes that 'All clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), never from the utility pole centerline or pole structure' and warns that 'Measuring from pole centerline instead of the conductor results in understated clearances and code violations.' Since no dimensions are shown on the plans at all, there is no evidence that the applicant is measuring from the outside conductor versus the pole.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Measurement Methodology section: 'Profile plans must show dimension lines originating at the conductor location, not at the pole. [This is critical.]' The complete absence of clearance dimensions means there is no opportunity to verify that dimensions originate from the conductor rather than the pole. This is a fundamental documentation failure that prevents verification of compliance. Without at least one dimension showing the measurement methodology and origin point (outside conductor), compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Clearance dimensions are not shown on any plan sheets. When clearance dimensions are eventually provided, they must originate from the outside (outermost) conductor, not from the utility pole centerline. Dimension lines should clearly identify the conductor location and show measurement to the building edge or feature being evaluated.

applicableAreas: Landscape plantings near overhead distribution conductors at Valley View Road frontage and site perimeter
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) depicts the overhead electric (OHE) utility line running along the southern/Valley View Road boundary. The vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms that 'There are several proposed trees located along the bottom boundary line, in close proximity to the -OHE- line' and notes that trees are marked with functional type codes (M for mitigation tree, PL for parking lot tree, P for parking buffer point tree). However, 'Specific botanical species are not labeled on this sheet' and 'There are no specific dimensions or distance callouts explicitly stating the distance from these trees to the overhead electric line.' The landscape calculations sheet (Sheet 35) shows proposed plantings: Cedar Elm (10 trees), Live Oak (2 trees), Mexican Redbud (6 trees), Texas Mountain Laurel (2 trees), and various shrubs and groundcover. However, there is no cross-reference between the species list and the landscape plan to identify which species are being planted near the overhead lines, nor is there any notation confirming these species are Utility Compatible (UC) per ECM Appendix F.
findings.reasoning: The grouping states: 'Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors are from Utility Compatible Shade Trees list' and 'ECM Appendix F "UC" column (utility-compatible trees generally mature height ≤20 feet marked "UC").' The grouping further notes: 'Common Violation Pattern: Non-utility-compatible trees beneath lines: Landscape plan shows large trees beneath or within 10 feet of overhead lines; species not from Utility Compatible list in ECM Appendix F.' The landscape plan fails to: (1) identify which specific proposed tree species are located within 10 feet of the overhead distribution line, (2) provide distance callouts showing lateral distance from proposed trees to the conductor, and (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet are marked as Utility Compatible in ECM Appendix F. Without this information, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: The landscape plan shows trees proposed near overhead electric distribution lines but does not identify the botanical species for trees in proximity to the OHE line or provide distance annotations showing lateral clearances. Landscape plan must be revised to: (1) call out the specific tree species being planted in areas near the overhead line (refer to tree species list on Sheet 35), (2) show lateral distance dimensions from proposed trees to the outside conductor, (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet of the overhead distribution conductor are from the Utility Compatible trees list per ECM Appendix F, or (4) demonstrate all proposed trees are planted beyond the 10-foot clearance zone.

applicableAreas: General notes on cover sheet or site plan sheets
findings.observation: The cover sheet (Sheet 1) and general notes sheet (Sheet 3) were reviewed in detail. Sheet 1 contains standard project information, Fire Department requirements, and administrative notes, but no mention of a 48-hour notification requirement to Austin Energy. Sheet 3 contains comprehensive notes about utilities, construction sequence, benchmarks, fire department requirements, and electric transmission clearances, but no explicit note requiring the owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy 48 hours before work near high-voltage overhead lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) similarly contains site plan release notes but no mention of the 48-hour notification requirement. While Sheet 9's release notes (Block 7) reference general utility relocation responsibility (Item 4: 'The owner is responsible for all costs of relocation of, or damage to, utilities' and Item 5: 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date'), there is no specific note stating that 'owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' as required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
findings.reasoning: The grouping's Documentation Requirements section explicitly states: '48-hour notification plan note: Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' The grouping further lists under Common Violation Patterns: 'Missing 48-hour notification note: Site has overhead lines and construction staging area adjacent, but no plan notes addressing notification requirement.' Since overhead electric facilities clearly exist on and adjacent to this site, and construction is planned adjacent to these lines, the required notification note must be prominently displayed on the plans.
findings.comment: Plans do not include required note stating that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. Add this requirement to the cover sheet general notes or site plan release notes in a location where all contractors and the owner will see it during project execution.
